items.summary: In this episode of WIRED's Uncanny Valley, hosts Zoë Schiffer and Leah Feiger examine how Elon Musk's America PAC allocated over $260 million to influence the 2026 Senate races, noting that the group spent more than twice as much opposing Democrats as supporting Republicans. The hosts also discuss the growing prominence of effective altruism within the AI safety community, highlighting how the Trump administration has labeled the philosophy a dangerous ideology. Finally, the episode covers backlash against designer Jessica Hische for accepting a $12,500 contract to create Meta's Muse logo, illustrating tensions between commercial work and AI ethics. The hosts provide context on these topics through interviews and analysis, offering insights into the intersection of technology, politics, and philosophy.
items.title: Podcast hosts discuss Elon Musk's election spending and AI safety debates

items.summary: Anthropic updated its usage policy on Thursday to explicitly prohibit prolonged verbal abuse of its AI model, Claude, as well as election interference and weapons software. The new rules target extreme cases of cruelty toward the model, distinguishing them from common user frustration or research. Additionally, the policy forbids deceptive campaigns, such as running fake accounts or disrupting democratic processes.
items.title: Anthropic Updates Policy to Ban Model Abuse and Election Interference

items.summary: OpenAI released hundreds of claimed solutions to difficult math problems, but the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI) stated the lab fell short of field standards regarding human understanding. While OpenAI followed some principles, only 10 of 719 manuscripts included chain-of-thought releases, and just 42% of proofs were formalized. A new paper highlighted discrepancies between natural language explanations and formal code for a Navier-Stokes problem. Mathematicians, including Terence Tao and Melanie Wood, argue that AI outputs lack the necessary human engagement and peer review required for the broader community to trust and utilize the results effectively.
items.title: OpenAI Math Solutions Fall Short of Community Standards

items.summary: David Gerald, president of the Securities Investors Association (Singapore), argues that new SGX RegCo listing rules effective Jan 1, 2027, are only half the solution for better governance. While companies must comply with enhanced requirements on remuneration and dividends, Gerald emphasizes that shareholders must actively use this information. He warns against treating engagement as a box-ticking exercise at annual general meetings. Instead, investors should examine remuneration structures, question capital allocation decisions, and engage continuously throughout the year. Gerald states that rules alone cannot create an engaged shareholder culture; real value emerges only when investors actually use the meaningful information provided by companies to hold management accountable.
items.title: Shareholders Must Act on New SGX Disclosure Rules

items.summary: US stocks dipped on Oct 8 as crude prices surged due to Middle East tensions and reduced US output, while semiconductor stocks slumped. The Nasdaq closed with the steepest percentage loss, followed by the S&P 500. Chipmakers, which have soared over 80% so far this year, were clear underperformers on the day, falling 3. 4% in the wake of a report from the Financial Times that OpenAI’s annualised revenues were US$20 billion less than the company previously signalled.
items.title: US Stocks Dip as Crude Prices Jump and Chip Stocks Weigh

items.summary: Databricks has introduced Funke, a successor to its open-source Smolder library, designed to parse HL7v2 healthcare messaging standards directly into native Spark types. While Smolder, released in 2021, served as a foundational tool, Funke is rebuilt to integrate cleanly with modern Databricks platform features like Unity Catalog and Declarative Automation Bundles. Funke aims to provide lossless, structured access to clinical data without the latency or detail loss associated with converting to FHIR or using third-party engines. It supports all HL7 message types and versions, allowing organizations to maintain full data fidelity within their lakehouse architecture.
items.title: Databricks Introduces Funke for Native HL7v2 Parsing on the Lakehouse

items.summary: As coding agents increasingly handle development tasks, traditional shared database setups create risks of conflict and data exposure. Lakebase Postgres addresses this by enabling database branching, allowing each agent to operate in an isolated environment similar to Git worktrees for code. This architecture supports copy-on-write storage, scale-to-zero capabilities, and independent schema migrations without affecting other agents. The approach facilitates safe testing, debugging, and validation against production-like data while mitigating the risks of concurrent agent operations. A practical workflow involves creating ephemeral branches for pull requests, running automated tests, and retiring branches once changes are merged.
items.title: Lakebase Enables Database Branching for Coding Agents

items.summary: Sasha Rakhlin, Director of MIT's Statistics and Data Science Center, outlines a strategy for universities to navigate the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence in academia. He notes that AI capabilities are advancing quickly, with models now solving complex mathematical problems and generating research results. Rakhlin argues that departments must rethink academic credit and training, focusing on intellectual responsibility and the formulation of questions rather than just polished outputs. He proposes that universities build shared AI research infrastructure to preserve tacit knowledge, capture negative results, and foster collaboration. This approach, he suggests, will allow institutions to pursue long-term scientific goals while maintaining technological independence and recognizing diverse contributions from researchers and students.
items.title: Sasha Rakhlin Outlines Path for AI in Academia

items.summary: The Public Transport Council (PTC) implemented a 7% fare adjustment, deferring 7.7% to future reviews supported by $200 million in 2027 subsidies. Measures include unchanged fares for Workfare cardholders, capped increases for concession groups, and expanded Public Transport Vouchers. The PTC states these steps maintain affordability while ensuring financial sustainability amidst rising costs.
items.title: PTC Balances Fare Affordability with System Sustainability

items.summary: Early results of the Beverage Container Return Scheme show over 48 million containers returned between April 1 and Sept 27, diverting 823 tonnes of material from incineration. The National Environment Agency and BCRS Ltd state they will monitor outcomes to improve effectiveness. CEO Stephanie Yip and Group Director Chan Chin Kai emphasize assessing the scheme based on environmental outcomes and ground experience.
items.title: Early results of drink container return scheme show high returns

items.summary: Developers preparing CAD assets for robotics simulation must configure materials, collision geometry, and physics properties beyond simple geometry conversion. NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, guided by SimReady Foundation specifications, offer a structured workflow where Frontier AI models assist in interpreting reference materials and executing tool calls. A walkthrough demonstrates this process using an ABB YuMi robot and GPT-6 Astra. The workflow involves five steps, including validation against SimReady requirements and a final pick-and-place task. While the simulation successfully demonstrated behavior under tested conditions, results may vary depending on the specific AI model and prompts used, and parameters were often estimated rather than calibrated against physical measurements.
items.title: NVIDIA and Frontier AI Models Streamline Robotics Simulation Asset Preparation

items.summary: Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to assemble assets and connect physics for creating simulations. These applications help explore scenarios, investigate failures, and improve designs. For instance, Frank DeLise used an AI agent to build an interactive warehouse simulator, while Doyub Kim created a reusable autonomous-vehicle testing environment based on San Francisco's Market Street. Other projects include refining digital twins for sensors, testing robot skills in sports simulations, and assembling an International Space Station model in a browser. Developers direct these AI agents through natural-language instructions to generate code and refine simulations based on specific metrics and physical constraints.
items.title: Developers Use Frontier AI Agents to Build Simulations With NVIDIA Omniverse

items.summary: A developer utilized an AI agent named ML Intern to create seven custom models in a few days. The process involved generating prompts, defining datasets, and setting strict budget limits. Projects included a citrus disease detection model, a style transfer LoRA named Huggy, and a camera-angle LoRA. The developer reported total compute costs ranging from USD 1.90 to USD 37 across various projects. Each model was trained on specific datasets and evaluated before publication on the Hugging Face Hub.
items.title: Developer Creates Custom AI Models Using ML Intern Agent

items.summary: Kate Collardson of the Solar Service of Colorado notes that aesthetic concerns remain a barrier to solar roof adoption. While Tesla's withdrawal from the market sent shockwaves through the industry, companies like Freesuns continue to expand, with CEO Deborah Learoyd estimating sales growth of 20–30% since 2019. However, solar roofs face challenges including higher costs, lower efficiency due to heat and size, and complex installation requiring specialized labor. Ben Graves of Sunsave suggests price remains a significant deterrent for UK consumers. Despite these hurdles, proponents argue solar roofs offer unique benefits for historic buildings and can generate additional electricity. Learoyd remains optimistic, believing embedded solar will eventually become standard for those with the means.
items.title: Why Solar Roofs Struggle Despite Growing Interest

items.summary: Firmus Technologies cancelled its planned ASX listing, aiming to be Australia's largest since Telstra in 1997, after failing to generate investor demand for its AI datacentre business. The company, backed by Nvidia and others, valued at $44bn, will now seek private funding. Shares in investor Maas Group fell over 20% following the news.
items.title: Firmus Cancels Record ASX Listing Amid Investor Doubt

items.summary: Meta's business continues to thrive despite significant challenges to Mark Zuckerberg's reputation and the company's public image. While Zuckerberg faced criticism during a recent keynote, Meta's products are experiencing rising usage, with app adoption increasing 3% year-on-year and second-quarter revenue up 28%. The company has navigated numerous legal battles, including a $18bn settlement with 48 US states and a $942m fine, yet its stock price has surged. Critics suggest Meta has become a 'Teflon' company, where scandals bounce off its operations. However, the company's pivot to AI, exemplified by the new Muse assistant, faces scrutiny over privacy concerns. Despite these issues, Meta's financial performance remains robust, driven by its advertising business and strategic investments in AI infrastructure.
items.title: Meta's Business Booms Despite Zuckerberg's Reputation Crisis

items.summary: The UK's data watchdog, the ICO, is investigating a sharp rise in complaints regarding 'robo calls' that ask recipients to add callers on WhatsApp. These calls are suspected to lead to recruitment scams. In September, the ICO received over 3,600 complaints, a five-year high. Andy Curry, the ICO's head of criminal investigations, stated that millions of people are likely receiving these messages, suggesting the reported complaints represent only a small proportion of the total affected.
items.title: UK watchdog investigates spike in WhatsApp recruitment scam calls

items.summary: Firmus, an Australian AI data centre operator backed by Nvidia, shelved its initial public offering on October 9 due to recent market volatility. The company stated it will now pursue capital from private markets and consider alternative public and private options.
items.title: Firmus Shelves IPO Amid Market Volatility

items.summary: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue is approximately $20 billion lower than previously indicated, based on financial documents shared with investors. OpenAI declined to comment immediately, and Reuters could not independently verify the report. The discrepancy stems from differing calculation methods between OpenAI and its rival, Anthropic, regarding cloud partner revenue.
items.title: OpenAI Revenue Lower Than Expected, FT Reports

items.summary: The World Trade Organization forecasts global goods trade will grow 3.9% this year, attributing the rise to booming AI trade offsetting Middle East conflicts. AI-related goods drove 47% of growth in the first half of 2026 despite representing only 15% of total trade. The WTO's chief economist noted that strong investment in AI infrastructure has outweighed the negative impact of the regional conflict on commerce.
items.title: WTO Predicts AI Trade Growth Will Offset Middle East Disruptions

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India clarified that individuals do not need to report personal import or export transactions under new FEMA regulations effective October 1. Officials stated this applies regardless of transaction amount, addressing confusion for freelancers and content creators. Small exporters may use self-declaration for shipments up to ₹10 lakh per bill, while banks handle reporting on the IEDPMS platform.
items.title: RBI Clarifies FEMA Rules on Personal Transaction Reporting

items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd announced an interim dividend of Rs 12 per share for the financial year 2026-27 on October 08, 2026. The company also released quarterly earnings for the period ending September 30, 2026. The record date for eligible shareholders is set for October 14, 2026.
items.title: TCS Announces Q2 Interim Dividend and Quarterly Earnings

items.summary: Elon Musk blamed "certain oligarchs" for preventing Starlink from entering India, a claim New Delhi dismissed as baseless. Musk questioned if Mukesh Ambani is India's real boss, noting that Jio and Airtel control 80% of the telecom market. The tech billionaire has frequently litigated regulatory disputes online, including recent actions against EU regulators and Delta CEO regarding Starlink and in-flight internet contracts.
items.title: Elon Musk Accuses Indian Oligarchs of Blocking Starlink Access Amid Market Dispute

items.summary: The State government has taken control of the $150 million Sydney Town Hall Square project. The planned $94 million plaza in front of Sydney Town Hall is now classified as a State Significant Development, subjecting it to a new approval process. The Independent Planning Commission determined the project could deliver significant public and economic benefits.
items.title: State Government Assumes Control of Sydney Town Hall Square Development

items.summary: WA Police are investigating the death of a man found at a residence on Nye Way in Orelia, Perth's southern suburbs. Officers were called to the scene around 2:20pm following reports of a serious incident. A second man known to the deceased was taken into custody. The Homicide Squad is leading the ongoing investigation, while police confirmed the incident is contained and there is no threat to public safety.
items.title: WA Police Investigate Death in Perth After Serious Incident Report

items.summary: Prof Peter Fonagy's review rejects the 'snowflake generation' narrative, stating that rising mental health issues among young people are real and driven by social factors like pandemic disruption and housing insecurity. While acknowledging a risk of overdiagnosis, the report emphasizes that diagnosis access creates unfairness and calls for early support rather than relying on clinical labels.
items.title: Mental Health Review Debunks 'Snowflake' Youth Caricature

items.summary: An NHS England review reports that mental distress has increased substantially across the population, affecting everyday functioning. The report notes that one in four 16- to 24-year-olds now have a common mental disorder, up from one in six in 1993. While severe mental illness rates remain stable, the cost of mental ill health stands at £300bn a year. The review warns that continuing current practices is unsustainable and recommends shifting from a diagnostic labelling model to a flexible, needs-led system. It also calls for prioritizing patients with the highest needs over a first-come-first-served approach.
items.title: NHS England review finds mental distress rising and calls for system overhaul

items.summary: On World Octopus Day, reports highlighted new findings about octopuses. Researchers described a fossilized jawbone of the extinct Nanaimoteuthis haggarti, suggesting it reached 6.6 to 18.6 meters in length. The species likely roamed seas between 100 million and 72 million years ago. Additionally, a new blue octopus species, Microeledone galapagensis, was confirmed in the Galapagos, though questions remain about its short arms.
items.title: New Discoveries Reveal Giant Ancient Octopus and New Species

items.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the execution of Nidal Hasan, a former Army major convicted of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be livestreamed. Hegseth stated the public would be able to watch the event to demonstrate serious consequences for such attacks. The execution is scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, marking the first military firing squad execution since 1945. While Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell confirmed President Trump approved the recommendation, legal experts like John Mills and Deborah Denno question the legal precedent and potential for appellate review to delay the event.
items.title: Pentagon Announces Livestreamed Firing Squad Execution of Nidal Hasan

items.summary: Elon Musk questioned whether Mukesh Ambani is the real boss of India after the government denied claims that oligarchs blocked Starlink's entry. Musk stated that opposition hurts the least-served and highlighted Starlink's presence in over 165 countries. Rahul Gandhi responded to Musk's comments on social media. Meanwhile, Reliance Jio and Eutelsat OneWeb await regulatory approvals for their satellite services in India.
items.title: Elon Musk Questions Ambani's Influence on Starlink Entry in India

items.summary: The Donald Trump administration has suspended Microsoft and several major technology and IT services companies, including Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant, Adobe, and Capgemini, from the US Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program. Vice President JD Vance announced the move on October 8, accusing these firms of abusing the system to replace American workers with cheaper foreign labor. The administration stated it would not accept new or process pending PERM applications for these entities, citing the exploitation of foreign-worker programs at the expense of US employees. PERM is a labor-certification step in the employment-based green-card process administered by the US Department of Labor.
items.title: Trump Administration Suspends Major Tech Firms from US Green-Card Program

items.summary: JD Vance claims Microsoft has abused the permanent labor certification program, alleging it laid off 6,000 American workers while utilizing 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. Vance states the company requested 3 million foreign workers. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling supports these figures, noting Microsoft received over 230,000 H-1B approvals and 100,000 permanent certifications, leading to suspensions alongside Adobe and Cognizant.
items.title: Vance Accuses Microsoft of Labor Fraud Amid Immigration Crackdown

items.summary: Amazon India reported a 100% year-on-year increase in order volume for its Great India Festival 2026, driven by strong demand for premium products. Director Aman Deep Lohan noted that consumer sentiment exceeded expectations, with significant sales in categories like beauty, fashion, and large appliances, supported by affordability levers such as no-cost EMI options.
items.title: Amazon India Reports Record Order Volume Growth at Festival

items.summary: TCS reported a 15% year-on-year profit increase to Rs 13,884 crore in Q2, driven by broad-based international growth and AI initiatives. Revenue rose 11% to Rs 73,188 crore, with annualised AI revenue reaching $3.1 billion. CEO K Krithivasan highlighted transformation partnerships, including deals with Porsche and Best Buy, while maintaining strong cash generation despite weak IT demand.
items.title: TCS Reports Q2 Profit Rise Amid AI Growth and Strategic Wins

items.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka urged the GST Council to ensure proposed reforms do not harm state revenues, warning Telangana could lose over ₹800 crore annually from motor vehicle changes. Speaking at the 57th meeting, he requested full financial impact assessments before implementation and highlighted that GST comprises 35% of Telangana's tax revenue. He also called for regional GST offices in Hyderabad and measures against tax evasion.
items.title: Telangana Finance Minister Urges GST Council to Protect State Revenue

items.summary: Condolences poured in for the demise of veteran actor and producer Nana Patekar on Thursday. Andhra Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, and others condoled the passing, recalling his remarkable contribution to Indian cinema. Naidu stated he was deeply saddened, noting his performances would be remembered for generations. The Andhra Pradesh Film Development Corporation also paid rich tributes during a board meeting in Vijayawada.
items.title: Condolences Pour In For Veteran Actor Nana Patekar

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed Jharkhand to revisit its DGP appointment regulations, stating they prima facie violated the Prakash Singh judgement. The court issued a notice to Tadasha Singh, appointed a day before retirement, and ordered her appointment set aside if regulations are annulled. It granted her a hearing opportunity. The Centre argued the 2025 amendment removed tenure requirements, while Jharkhand contested selective targeting.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Jharkhand to Revisit DGP Appointment Rules

items.summary: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026 came into force on October 8, mandating that 50% of inspector general posts, at least 67% of additional director general posts, and 100% of director general and special director general-level posts in CAPFs be filled by IPS officers on deputation. This follows a Supreme Court direction from May 2025 for a gradual reduction in IPS deputation, which the Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan defended as lawful. While CAPF cadre officers oppose the move as career-blocking, the government maintains that IPS officers are crucial for coordination between the Centre and states.
items.title: IPS Quota for Senior CAPF Posts Comes into Force

items.summary: Malaysia's prime minister contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto regarding severe haze choking Kuala Lumpur caused by wildfires. Air quality in the capital reached 'very unhealthy' levels, ranking it the most polluted city globally. Schools in Johor closed, affecting about 617,000 students. While officials discussed regional cooperation and cloud seeding, civil groups called for stronger laws to hold companies accountable for environmental damage.
items.title: Malaysian PM Contacts Indonesian President Over Haze Crisis

items.summary: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav of Madhya Pradesh criticized the Congress party and Rahul Gandhi for questioning the Election Commission following electoral losses, urging introspection instead. He pointed to Congress victories in Kerala and Himachal Pradesh as evidence of a fair democratic process. Conversely, Opposition leader Umang Singhar accused the government of authoritarianism and claimed the Election Commission acts as a BJP agent, demanding the government listen to Rahul Gandhi's voice for democracy.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh CM Calls for Congress Introspection Amid Electoral Debate

items.summary: Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava stated that IGST exemptions on gold, silver, and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies expire on March 31, 2026. Effective April 1, 2026, these imports will attract a 3% IGST to ensure tax parity. This follows government concerns over forex outgo and a call by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to curb non-essential imports.
items.title: India extends IGST exemption on precious metal imports for banks until March 2026

items.summary: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that the Union government will release a consultation paper on AI safety within a month, focusing on deepfakes and societal harms. Speaking at a World Bank event, he emphasized the need for a techno-legal solution and industry collaboration. The government is also empanelling AI models for public use and issuing tenders for GPUs.
items.title: India Plans AI Safety Regulations and Industry Consultation

items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh West Zone Electricity Distribution Company provided permanent electricity connections to 8,735 farmers in the Malwa-Nimar region for an initial fee of Rs 5. Managing director Anup Kumar Singh stated that the streamlined online process aims to offer quick relief and reduce financial burdens. The initiative covers multiple districts, including Indore and Ujjain, as part of the state's Year of Farmers' Welfare priorities.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh Provides Low-Cost Electricity Connections to Farmers
